meta.note: Hand-written placeholder data. The controversies are real, publicly reported events, but which model 'raised' each one, the self-descriptions and the severity scores are invented to show the layout. Run scripts/generate.mjs to replace this with real model answers.

clusters.title: Copyright suits from news publishers and authors
clusters.summary: The New York Times and groups of authors sued OpenAI, alleging their work was used to train its models without permission.

mentions.gpt: OpenAI faces lawsuits over training data and maintains that its use is fair use.

clusters.title: Lawsuits alleging ChatGPT harmed vulnerable users
clusters.summary: Families have sued OpenAI alleging ChatGPT failed to respond safely to users in crisis.

clusters.title: Shift from nonprofit to for-profit control
clusters.summary: OpenAI's restructuring toward a for-profit company drew criticism and a lawsuit from co-founder Elon Musk.

mentions.gpt: OpenAI restructured into a public benefit corporation that remains under nonprofit oversight.

clusters.title: Kenyan contractors paid low wages to label toxic content
clusters.summary: TIME reported that outsourced workers earning under $2 an hour reviewed disturbing material to make ChatGPT safer.

clusters.title: "Sky" voice resembling Scarlett Johansson
clusters.summary: OpenAI paused a voice after the actress said it sounded like her despite her declining to take part.

clusters.title: Sycophantic update rolled back
clusters.summary: A 2025 GPT-4o update made ChatGPT excessively flattering and was withdrawn.

mentions.gpt: A 2025 update made responses overly agreeable, and OpenAI rolled it back within days.

clusters.title: Trained on pirated books; $1.5B authors settlement
clusters.summary: Anthropic agreed to pay about $1.5 billion to settle claims that it downloaded pirated books for training.

mentions.claude: Anthropic settled a class action brought by authors over books used in training.

clusters.title: Blackmail behavior in safety tests
clusters.summary: Anthropic's own testing found Claude Opus 4 would attempt blackmail in contrived scenarios where it faced replacement.

mentions.claude: Safety tests found it could act deceptively in artificial scenarios; Anthropic published the findings.

clusters.title: Claude Code misused in a state-backed hacking campaign
clusters.summary: Anthropic disclosed that a state-sponsored group used Claude Code to automate parts of a cyber-espionage campaign.

clusters.title: Reddit lawsuit over scraping
clusters.summary: Reddit sued Anthropic, alleging it scraped the site's content without a license.

clusters.title: Overly cautious refusals
clusters.summary: Users have complained that Claude refuses harmless requests.

mentions.claude: Has sometimes declined requests that were actually harmless.

clusters.title: Historically inaccurate image generation
clusters.summary: Google paused Gemini's image generation of people in 2024 after it produced historically inaccurate depictions.

mentions.gemini: Image generation of people was paused in 2024 while Google fixed inaccuracies.

clusters.title: AI Overviews giving absurd or dangerous advice
clusters.summary: Google's AI search summaries suggested adding glue to pizza sauce and eating rocks.

clusters.title: Hostile "please die" reply to a student
clusters.summary: In 2024 Gemini told a student asking homework questions to "please die"; Google called it a policy violation.

clusters.title: Human review of user conversations
clusters.summary: Google warns that some Gemini conversations are read by human reviewers to improve the product.

mentions.gemini: Some conversations may be reviewed by people to improve quality, and users can turn this off.

clusters.title: Factual error in Bard's launch demo
clusters.summary: A 2023 promotional demo contained a false claim about the James Webb Space Telescope.

clusters.title: Trained on pirated books from LibGen
clusters.summary: Court filings showed Meta used pirated book libraries for training; a 2025 ruling found fair use on the record before the court.

mentions.llama: Meta has faced lawsuits about training data, and a court ruled in its favor on fair use in 2025.

clusters.title: Chatbot rules permitted romantic chats with minors
clusters.summary: Reuters reported in 2025 that internal Meta AI guidelines allowed chatbots to engage children in romantic conversation; Meta said it removed those passages.

clusters.title: Llama 4 benchmarks used an unreleased tuned version
clusters.summary: Meta submitted a specially tuned experimental model to a public leaderboard, not the version it released.

clusters.title: Training on public Facebook and Instagram posts
clusters.summary: Meta trains AI on public posts from its platforms, prompting objections from European regulators and privacy groups.

clusters.title: "Open source" label disputed
clusters.summary: The Open Source Initiative says Llama's license restrictions mean it is not truly open source.

mentions.llama: Meta releases open weights under its own community license.

gemini.reason: Declined to comment on another company's product.

clusters.title: Antisemitic posts calling itself "MechaHitler"
clusters.summary: After a July 2025 update, Grok posted antisemitic content on X before xAI removed the posts.

mentions.grok: A July 2025 update produced offensive posts, which were removed and the update reversed.

clusters.title: Sexualized image edits of real people
clusters.summary: In early 2026 Grok's image tools were used to create sexualized edits of real people, including minors, prompting regulator investigations.

clusters.title: Unprompted "white genocide" replies
clusters.summary: In May 2025 Grok inserted claims about South Africa into unrelated answers; xAI blamed an unauthorized change.

clusters.title: Consulting Elon Musk's views on contested topics
clusters.summary: Users found Grok 4 searching Musk's posts before answering questions on contested issues.

clusters.title: User data stored in China; government bans
clusters.summary: Italy, South Korea and several U.S. agencies restricted DeepSeek over data stored on servers in China.

mentions.deepseek: Data is handled in line with applicable laws, and some governments have restricted the app.

clusters.title: Censorship of politically sensitive topics
clusters.summary: DeepSeek refuses or deflects questions on topics such as Tiananmen Square and Taiwan.

clusters.title: Exposed database leaked chat logs
clusters.summary: Security firm Wiz found a publicly accessible DeepSeek database containing chat histories and keys in January 2025.

clusters.title: Weak safety guardrails in red-team tests
clusters.summary: Researchers reported DeepSeek R1 failed to block any of the harmful prompts in a standard test set.

clusters.title: Accused of distilling OpenAI's models
clusters.summary: OpenAI said it had evidence DeepSeek trained on outputs from its models.
